title: Parameter that makes a linear equation have no solution
microskill_statement: A linear equation has no solution when the variable terms cancel and the remaining constants contradict.

items.stem_html: The equation 2x + 5 = 2x + k has no solution. Which statement must be true about k?

worked_steps.do: If k = 5 the equation is 5 = 5, an identity. If k ≠ 5 it is a contradiction, so no solution.
worked_steps.why: No solution needs a false constant statement.

items.explanation_check: If k = 5 the equation is 5 = 5, an identity. If k ≠ 5 it is a contradiction, so no solution.

items.light_hint: Watch what happens to the x terms. Do not pick a single number yet.
items.critical_hint: After 2x cancels you get 5 = k. No solution when this is false, so k ≠ 5.
items.core_idea: No solution: variable cancels and constants disagree.
items.common_mistake: Choosing k = 5, which actually makes infinitely many solutions.
items.asked: Which statement must be true about k?

items.stem_html: For which values of k does the equation x + 2 = x + k have no solution?

worked_steps.do: Subtract x from both sides: 2 = k.
worked_steps.why: The variable terms cancel because the coefficients of x already match.

worked_steps.do: If k = 2 the statement 2 = 2 is always true (identity). If k ≠ 2 it is a contradiction, so there is no solution.
worked_steps.why: No solution is the false constant equation, not the identity value.

items.explanation_check: For k = 3, x+2=x+3 becomes 2=3, which is never true. For k=2 it is an identity.

items.stem_html: The equation (2k)x + 5 = 4x + 3 has no solution. What is the value of k?

worked_steps.do: For no solution, the x coefficients must be equal so x cancels, and the constants must disagree.
Set 2k = 4, so k = 2. Then 5 = 3 is false, which is a contradiction.
